title: This Spider Spins a Web 82 Feet Across a River. Tougher Than Kevlar

scenes.text: This spider spins a web 82 feet across a river.
Darwin's bark spider, Madagascar. Smaller than your thumbnail.
She fires a line into the wind, it catches the far bank, and she builds a web the size of a parking space.
The silk is the toughest biological material ever tested. Ten times tougher than Kevlar.
Twice as tough as any other spider silk on Earth.
One web traps 30 insects at a time. 82 feet. From a spider the size of your thumbnail.

description:
Darwin's bark spider, discovered in Madagascar and described in 2010, builds the largest orb webs known: its bridge lines reach 25 metres (82 feet) across rivers and lakes, with webs up to 2.8 square metres.
Its silk is the toughest biological material ever measured, more than twice as tough as any other spider silk and over ten times tougher than Kevlar by the same measure. A single web can hold around 30 insects at once.
Would you walk under this web? Comment below.
first_comment: The record 25-metre line was spun across a lake; typical river webs are 10 to 14 metres. Would you rather face a spider or a snake?
